and having beheld them, the Soul of the Universe questioned them together with his beloved.
"Where will you two brahmins stay, and what will you do to pass the time?
When Samba asked this, Śuka, with a joyful mind, replied right then and there:
"Fortunate as I am, I remain here constantly in your garden, taking refuge upon a branch of the Kṛtamāla tree."
The swan also, having bowed again to the Lord with palms joined in reverence, spoke:
"I am one who wanders through the worlds of Brahmā and Viṣṇu, as well as among the guardians of the quarters."
O Lord, by the power of your abundant merit, you have come here to this garden,
where you always drink the nectar-like water from the middle of the pond.
I now dwell here, constantly praising the eternal majesty of the waters that reside within the matted locks of your wife.
To that swan and the parrot who were speaking thus, the Lord of the worlds said,
"Go," and having spoken to them, he dismissed them with a smile.
Then the queen, rising from her seat in great anger, said to the Lord:
"How can you call me your wife on the basis of Haṃsa’s words?"
Joy, laughter, and the words "Excellent! Excellent! emerged from your mouth;
having gone a short distance, they dissolved somewhere, gathering dust upon the ground.
She fashioned a puppet, and it rose up once more as if alive;
meanwhile, Mahādeva [beheld] the Mother of the World, who was filled with wrath.
Having consoled her and brought her back,
the Lord went to the inner apartments with those very dust particles with which the image of the goddess Umā had been fashioned at that time.
From that, the heaps of ash from the body of the burnt Manmatha became Durguṇa,
who has the form of a man and dwells near Kailāsa.
The lords of the Gaṇas, looking up at him, said: "You are the asura named Bhaṇḍa;
go, O wicked one, for you, the enemy of the gods, must not remain here."
Saying "I am finished with Asuras" in anger, that demon Bhaṇḍa departed.
Bhaṇḍāsura performed most terrible penance for ten million times ten thousand years out of extreme detachment, thereby pleasing the Lord of Creatures.
O Lord of the Gods, my enemies are the deities, including Hari, Brahmā, and the others.
Then, out of compassion for the Lord, I shall withdraw their powers;
by that means, they may find me dwelling within their hearts as they consume my power.
Thus he requested a boon from Tryambaka, the God of gods;
pleased by that austerity, the Lord then granted him every boon.
The asura Bhaṇḍa, having obtained the boon, was consuming the vital energy of all the gods,
including Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Indra, and the other chief deities.
The gods, including Indra, their vigor destroyed and devoid of passion for their own wives, were filled with despondency, wondering "What is this? yet the gods did not recognize him.
Desiring a remedy for this,
Brahmā, Hari, Hara, and the other lords of the directions were intensely devoted to the worship of Īśa.
Having worshipped the Lord with sixteen types of offerings at the Liṅga,
he then went to Mount Kailāsa and worshipped Śiva.
"O Lord, we have become devoid of energy; we do not know the cause of this.
To those speaking thus, headed by Hari and Brahmā, the Lord (Īśvara) replied:
Thus Bhaṇḍāsura, having taken your prowess, has entered his body.
p. 468) For that purpose, if I am to perform the sacrifice of universal withdrawal (*sarvasaṃhārayāga*), the consent of the Asuras is required; otherwise, it simply cannot be accomplished.
When all embodied beings have been offered as oblations into the sacrificial fire by my performance,
thereupon, by my command, some power of mine shall come into being.

"Having destroyed Bhaṇḍāsura, she will give birth to you; this which I have spoken to the gods is true and shall happen in an instant as before. Hearing these words of the god, the gods replied with the word "So be it."
"We are rendered powerless in hand and foot and utterly averse to women"—
thus spoke the Lord after the gods had been dismissed and had departed.
In his own great fire, he offered as sacrificial fuel the gods,
the sages, the hosts of ancestors, and others— the gandharvas, uragas, and rākṣasas.
Having seized humans, birds, cattle, and all that moves or is stationary in the world,
the Great Devourer himself was consecrated by Ambā into the fire.
When all things, both stationary and moving, have been offered without remainder;
From that fire there arose Śakti together with three eggs,
bearing a flower-arrow, a sugarcane bow, a goad, and a garland.
Having reached the feet of Mahādeva, Śakti prostrated herself and addressed him:
"O Lord of all beings, command me; what task must be done?"
To her who was speaking thus, the powerful Lord of Girijā said:
"The most terrible Bhaṇḍāsura is a devourer of his own kin."
"O Great Power, withdraw [this] quickly for the protection of all beings!
Then she too discharged a single arrow at him.
As soon as the demon Bhaṇḍāsura was suddenly slain by her with a single arrow, she withdrew her life-breaths from him at his command.
Immediately thereafter, the Ocean of Compassion commanded that Śakti:
"Once the three cosmic eggs have been created by you, [install] Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara."
Having united Mahālakṣmī, Ambikā, and Sarasvatī, the goddess of speech,
with their respective husbands, he [established] creation, preservation, and dissolution in due order.
Bearing that command of Śiva upon her head,
the Sovereign likewise brought forth three [beings] and their corresponding powers of a similar nature.
By means of those three qualities, he caused the functions of creation, preservation, and dissolution to be performed;
then, on another occasion, he assumed his own form as Kālāgnirudra.
By means of that one [form], the Lord himself, sometimes assuming the form of Viṣṇu, performs the activities of creating, protecting, and dissolving the world.
By means of that one [being], the Lord causes the acts of creation and so forth to be performed;
indeed, having assumed the form of Brahmā, he does so by means of that very one.
In every kalpa, the Lord, the Master of the Universe, creates, sustains, and destroys;
nevertheless, the Consort of Ambikā assumes his own form as Rudra.
Perceiving himself as non-different [from that], he always remains there;
in some kalpa, Brahmā, having propitiated the god Sadāśiva, [attains his state].
Hari himself indeed creates, maintains, and destroys the world;
yet in another kalpa, having thus propitiated Sadāśiva, he [attains his state].
"The Supreme Śruti states that the Lord, presiding over those three gods, sports by performing the creation, maintenance, and dissolution of the world at every kalpa.
Having propitiated the God of gods, [the gods], impelled by their respective egos..."
They perform all activities, such as creation and so forth, solely by their own command.
The name of Rudra’s form, its insignia, and its activity—
whatever is the name of Sadāśiva, no distinction exists between these two.
Having empowered others, Śiva himself bestows what is desired;
and as the Sovereign Lord, he issues commands to all, looking upon them with respect.
"I am indeed that Hara; there exists no difference between us two.
Having thus instructed them, the divine Śiva vanished from their sight.
Having obtained great enjoyments through that worship, those three gods also constantly perform the creation, maintenance, and destruction [of the world] individually.
From that time forward, they enjoyed vast pleasures— both those pertaining to Brahmā and those pertaining to Viṣṇu— as the glory of the worship of Śiva accumulated for them.
And those three experienced the fierce [state] born from the words [of the Lord], arising from the command of Īśvara,
as well as the supreme bliss of Śiva.
Bhaṇḍāsura was slain before Śiva by Śivā,
who then attained the status of a chief among Rudra’s attendants— a rank difficult even for the immortals to achieve.
Even today, she who was born from the sacrificial fire-pit and originated from a portion of Ambā remains in the presence of the Supreme Lord and his consort together with her attendants.
She who is celebrated as Tripurā, possessing flower-arrows and a bow of sugarcane,
having propitiated the Lord (Īśa), has become united with Śiva.
Thus, for the sake of the demon Bhaṇḍa, Śiva offered this entire world— including Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Indra, and the rest— into the fire of his own portion like sacrificial fuel in a fierce sacrifice;
and with his great power, together with the wife of Tripura, he caused the lord of demons, Bhaṇḍāsura, to be slain.
Just as he had fashioned all other gods, he once again created the entire universe through the Goddess.

Whatever fruit one might obtain by performing austerities with devotion at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean, on the slopes of the Himālayas, on Mount Meru, in Kāśī, on Vṛddhagiri, at Prayāga and Gayā, at Madhyārjuna, or in Naimiṣa— by worshipping Śaṅkara even once, one attains that fruit in its entirety.
By worshipping in the *liṅga*, one shall obtain that fruit; oh faultless lady, I shall now declare it to you.
All the vows, such as the Cāndrāyaṇa and others, have been performed by him according to the prescribed rules;
and by him, the worlds beginning with Bhūr have been conquered.
By whomsoever the worship of Śiva has been performed even once.
The ignorant one, desiring to cross over the sufferings of saṃsāra after experiencing them throughout thousands of births,
[should worship] Maheśa together with Bhavānī but once.
One should worship with devotion in a faultless *liṅga*.
For those who worship the *liṅga*, there is no dwelling in a womb,
no suffering of birth, and no fear of death; they attain divinity, lordship over the quarters, and the state of a sage.
O blameless one, the state of being the lord of gods is under his control.
Whatever has been ordained within the cosmic egg for the sake of enjoyment, in accordance with one's past merits,
that shall be accomplished by performing the worship of the Liṅga.
But it is even more supreme than the moon and the stars.
Whoever performs worship of Maheśa, whether out of a desire for worldly enjoyment or seeking the goals of human life,
shall obtain every fruit in accordance with their wish.
He sports before the Supreme Lord.
Whatever one may desire among sensual pleasures, by performing the worship of Śiva with that very intent, one indeed obtains it without effort;
for there is nothing blameless here that cannot be attained through the worship of the Lord.
And even that state which is so difficult to attain would not be accomplished.
For a living being devoid of worship there is no higher state; for a living being devoid of worship there is no liberation;
even the status of Brahmā, Indra, Viṣṇu, and the rest is not attained by one who lacks worship.
Without her, even after a thousand births.
O Goddess, the sovereignty of the Lord over the entire earth has been demonstrated through worship;
likewise, the attainment of the eightfold supernatural powers is not obtained anywhere else.
Delightful women with eyes as broad as lotus petals, houses endowed with auspiciousness,
and wealth sufficient for all desires belong to Śambhu.
Those who perform worship attain success in this faultless [state].
Having first worshipped with devotion a beautiful stone *liṅga* of Rudra, Hari [attained] that foremost and most difficult-to-attain Vaiṣṇava [state]. (p. 472)
I have not attained that supreme state which is desired.
Having propitiated the great liṅga of Maheśa, Lakṣmī obtained the chest of Hari as her dwelling;
thus the Creator became the maker of all.
And that Bhāratī was his beloved.
By worshipping the Liṅga, Indra became the lord of the thirty gods, and Śacī obtained him as her devoted husband; thus,
he is to be propitiated by all conscious beings.
O faultless one, that Lord of the Mountain is the form of Śiva together with Ambā.
The worship of Īśāna grants all desires, and the worship of Śivā shall likewise always be effective; therefore,
O faultless one, it may be performed by anyone whatsoever.
And Bhavānī and Parameśvara are to be worshipped.
Having worshipped [the Lord] at a divine liṅga established on earth by oneself, or at one fashioned from fine food, or even at a crystal one, or at a sacred ford, a mountain, or a forest;
He should not listen to any discourse pertaining to Yama.
Having worshipped with devotion the Supreme Lord, either with the *triyambaka* mantra, or with the *namaḥ śivāya* mantra accompanied by the *praṇava*.
Perhaps he might hear some story concerning Yama.
By the power of Maheśvara’s worship and likewise by the power of Ambikā’s devotion,
those who resemble Śiva shall remain in the presence of Śiva.
As many as nine or five Śakras play.
Austerities, sacrifices with abundant sacrificial fees,
and even the merit of reciting the *Raudra-sūkta* are not equal to [the merit of] constantly worshipping Maheśa preceded by devotion to Him.
One should propitiate Māra with the rites ending in the sacrifice to Ambikā.
Whether out of deceit, or from pride and greed, or even through casual association, or by mere chance—
those who bow to the Lord do not go to Yama.
By worshipping with the five-syllable mantra, they become liberated.
Longevity, health, extreme happiness,
enjoyments, sovereignty, excellent women, noble sons, a beloved wife, wealth, and everything else— [all these are attained].
They appear before those who worship Śiva.
They attained learning, beauty, noble lineage, the fulfillment of desired prosperity, a wife, and a pleasing residence;
they attained knowledge and the fruit of higher wisdom.
Worshipping Śiva, whose crest is the moon.
Even for one who propitiates Rudra with devotion for but a single day, the station of Maheśāna is bestowed;
what then need be said of those who worship Umēśa incessantly?
According to the prescribed ritual with the Śatarudra mantras.
Whether he be a Caṇḍāla, a Śvapaca, or even one who has fallen from grace, a cow-killer, or an ungrateful person—
if he worships Śaṅkara even once at the Liṅga while contemplating Śiva within his own heart,
he is liberated from millions of sins and shines like the sun released from the clouds.
This is the truth, this is the truth; O faultless one, I shall say this again and again to you.
Having attained this human birth which is so very difficult to find, that fool who does not perform worship of Īśāna makes that very life of his utterly fruitless.
For one who performs worship, that birth is indeed fruitful.
(474) By the worship of the Lord, even those guilty of great sins shall be liberated from their faults;
just as by the skill of a physician, the sick are quickly freed from their diseases.
When the Lord is thus pleased, what is there that cannot be accomplished?
I shall declare to you the secret essence of the scriptures: the practice of renunciation and the conquest of the senses;
know that there is nothing equal to the worship of Śiva.
That alone should always be practiced without fault.
Even a man who is burdened by evil, devoted to sin, or even associated with sinful people, is not defiled in his faultlessness,
just as a lotus leaf is not wetted by water.
Likewise, if one who worships Śaṅkara is [associated] with evildoers.
He who obtains the sight of the Lord as a boon in the morning attains a most exalted state; through the constant sight of the supreme Liṅga, he reaches that goal.
Though joined with sins, he becomes liberated here in this world.
Beholding the sin-destroying Linga of Umāpati at dawn grants heaven;
at midday it yields fruit equal to a horse-sacrifice;
and at evening, during the time of the sun's setting, its worship with the five-syllabled mantra removes the cycle of birth.
It yields desired fruit equal to that of the three times—past, present, and future—immediately, daily, and without flaw.
The sight and touch of the Lord, the most excellent one, by his two hands—
that linga which is most meritorious for us— [is supreme].
And one is not smeared by even ten million sins.
Whether one is a matricide, a patricide, a killer of cattle,
or a slayer of an embryo, a hero, or a guru—
if they worship the Liṅga of Maheśvara even without mantras, [they are purified].
Having touched that which is blameless, he would become pure.
Having then conceived that as his own characteristic mark, the pure one who is unworthy may touch everything;
the worthy one [does so] at the onset of the thirteenth night, during the twilight (pradoṣa).
[He saw] one whose neck was blue, adorned with garments, offerings, and armlets.
Having seen [Her] in that faultless form, one endowed with devotion is liberated from heaps of sins;
even a mass of evil accumulated over tens of thousands of births is destroyed.
By the mere sight of the Destroyer of Tripura,
[sin] perishes instantly; just as cotton is consumed by fire, so it is— how wonderful, O faultless one!
A man who kills a child, a father, a cow, a horse, a son, or a woman; a killer of a Śūdra or a mother;
one who speaks of the faults of others with malicious words; a stealer of jewels;
or a thief of the cattle or wealth of a deity or another person; or even a murderer—[these are the transgressors].
Upon seeing the linga of the Lord of Umā, one suddenly becomes purified and irreproachable.
Recollecting past lives, mastery of many sciences, possession of discernment, and sovereignty over the earth—
whether through fear or by the power of knowledge.
One attains [this] by beholding the Liṅga of the image of Īśvara.
The sight of the Lord brings about the destruction of evil; touching him bestows the status of being a member of Rudra’s retinue;
that sight shall grant the fruit of liberation.
Whoever, according to the prescribed rule and preceded by the recitation of Vedic mantras,
constantly performs the circumambulation of Śiva five times with devotion;
Furthermore, having once again performed a circumambulation with hymns of praise, one goes to a state where there is no further birth.
For every step a mortal takes toward the sight of the form of the Śiva-liṅga,
he shall obtain the merit of a horse sacrifice for each and every step.
And likewise when proceeding in circumambulation.
A student (*varṇin*) should circumambulate the left side, while an ascetic (*yati*) should do so on the right; both should perform it on both sides.

One dwelling in the stage of a twice-born householder (*vānaprastha*) and a householder (*gṛhastha*) should perform the circumambulation clockwise, keeping the bull-herd (*vṛṣagaṇa*), the bull (*vṛṣabha*), the Soma-thread (*somasūtra*), and the bull (*vṛṣa*) to their right.
Furthermore, that which is called "Caṇḍa," the thread (*sūtra*), "Caṇḍa," and the bull (*vṛṣabha*) must be performed during the *pradoṣa* [twilight] rites.
Having bowed again and again with prostrations and obeisances, [he performed] a circumambulation of Śambhu by moving around him on all sides.

Having bowed down one hundred thousand times to the left and the right, two hundred thousand times to the bull and the others, eighty million times with prostrations and circumambulations, and seventy million times to Śiva; thereafter, the entire outer enclosure is tenfold with the limbs [of the body]. There shall be ten [circumambulations] for the outermost circle.
Except during hymns of praise, he maintains silence; his gait is slow and measured, and his hands are joined in reverence upon his head.
The virtuous indeed say that there are seven circumambulations of the form of Śaṅkara’s Liṅga;
furthermore, each subsequent one should be ten times greater than the preceding.
Indeed, at every step, the fruit of sacrifice is surely attained.
Beholding, saluting, worshipping, circumambulating,
and offering libations to the Lord on a Saturday at dusk leads to the liberation from debt.
He is the blazing submarine fire within the ocean of worldly existence.
If one does not behold Hari at the time of dusk,
yet by negligence should see the Discus-bearer [at that time],
four things perish for that man.
Through the power of wisdom, [attain] long life and irreproachable fame.
If one does not behold Hari at the time of dusk when even a fraction of the thirteenth lunar day remains in the night,
there will be a loss of memory if one looks out of negligence.
There would be the destruction of the three [karmas] and the nine [subdivisions].
If, through negligence, one should especially see [the deity] at the onset of the night of the thirteenth day— that is, at the break of dawn—
then for twelve years, one will have the vigor of a bull.
The worship and prostration of Hari at the time of Pradoṣa.
One who is endowed with devotion should not perform the recitation or remembrance, nor the visualization, of that which is faultless;
for if one does not perform these acts, there is no loss of dharma.
They say that the worship of Viṣṇu is a task to be performed continuously.
Even at that time, O blameless one, except during the hour of dusk, one should perform the viewing, worship, and chanting of praises for the form of Nṛsiṃha.
Fire-offerings, recitation, and communal meals.
One should abandon the oil for recitation and association with Hari during the evening hours of the form of Nṛsiṃha;
for the world-renowned nature of Rudra is indeed established.
Therefore, the propitiation of the Lord [is necessary].
One who delights in the consecration of Śiva should perform it at the proper time according to the prescribed rules;
[regarding] that doctrine of division which will be explained in due order—
Having anointed [him] with oil, ghee, and curd.
One should perform the consecration with milk, or with sugarcane juice, with fragrant water along with coconut water and honey,
and also with pure water.
Having attained every desired accomplishment in its entirety.
One who possesses discernment, having examined with the vision of knowledge both the ultimate reality and the state of being the Lord of the Pramathas,
becomes liberated by devotion to Īśa upon attaining it.
Śambhu [washes away] the ten offenses with water.
An improper consecration [is remedied] by bathing in faultless water,
or by offering a hundred cows with their well-matured milk and curds;
[if done] with clarified butter, a thousand times, or perhaps ten thousand times.
He who should cause the daily bathing of the Śiva-liṅga form with ghee for one month,
having delivered ten million ancestors born of his own lineage, [attains the supreme state].
He rejoices on the peak of Mount Rājata,
having worshipped the Liṅga anointed with ghee by means of wheat flour and barley flour.
By rubbing with *bilva* leaves a linga or its pedestal that has been sprinkled with warm water, one becomes the donor of ten million cows.
[This applies to] the warm water of the pedestal...
And sprinkling, and rubbing with bilva leaves.
Whoever reverently bathes the Lord’s Liṅga with oil or ghee on the eighth day of the dark fortnight gains a merit equal to the gift of a thousand cows a thousand times over.
With fresh ghee and oils of black sesame.
He who bathes the Lord with white ash is purified from all sins accumulated over thousands, tens of thousands, and millions of kalpas.
Through devotion to the blameless one, he is liberated from sin.
Resplendent as a moonbeam, he rejoices like Śiva in the very orb of the moon;
[he who gives] ten thousand cows to those learned in the Vedas.
During a solar eclipse, together with gold and garments.
O blameless one, that fruit which is obtained by a donor through bathing a Liṅga with the fine milk of cows—
even a single bath of the Lord with curds— is [immeasurable].
Performing this, one indeed attains the divine station of Viṣṇu.
Or whoever should bathe the *iśaliṅga* with faultless honey and pure water using washed cloths, he shall go to the station of Agni.
Having bathed the Linga, he obtains his desires.
Having attained the state of Pracetas, he rejoices, serene,
amidst thousands of celestial damsels;
therefore, one should bathe you on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Kṛṣṇa.
On the day of the Moon, however, [one should bathe] with the milk of cows.
O blameless one, a man attains union with the divine *liṅga* of Maheśvara through devotion;
O blameless one, it is as if bathed in the water of a lotus stalk.
On the eighth lunar day, on a Sunday, and on a Saturday, [one should worship] at the Liṅga.
Through the attainment of union (sāyujya), he is established in the hand;
he is primarily white, drinking deeply from the lotus-stalk,
or else [he appears] on the eighth or fourteenth day of the dark fortnight.
The linga of Śiva [is smeared] with ghee and oil.
Or, by bathing [the deity] with honey, one leads him to union; he attains the *sāyujya* of Lord Hari.
Having bathed the *liṅga* of Maheśa with oil, [one attains the same].
And he attains union with the deity, along with three generations of his lineage.
Likewise, by means of the essence of sugarcane, he rejoices in that presence for ten million eons;
thus, he who bathes the Lord with excellent ghee on the days sacred to Śiva [attains this].
A man who visits the Liṅga of Hara— even if he has accumulated sins over hundreds of existences—

abandons them and, having become like Indra, attains the Silver Mountain (Kailāsa) along with ten million kinsmen; having attained his desired goal in all worlds, he becomes liberated in the stainless state.
Having bathed [the deity] with ghee, curd, honey, oil, and milk, and having offered one [portion] to the Goddess,
one should perform the bathing with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) upon the Lord’s liṅga.
The virtuous declare that it yields great fruit.
One should perform the Rudrābhiṣeka with waters purified by fine cloth, using the Śatarudriya hymns,
fifteen, eight, six, seven, or even ten times.
O blameless one, he would become a human being, Rudra.
With flowers and leaves grown on mountains or in the forest, produced in one's own garden, free from holes or insects, fresh, not fallen to the ground, and pure.
All forms of worship should be performed by human beings.
The worship of a liṅga with a single flower from an arka plant offered to a twice-born who knows the Vedas is equal to the gift of ten pieces of gold.
The virtuous declare them to be equal in being irreproachable.
A single *karavīra* flower is better than even a thousand *arka* flowers; indeed,
[a single *karavīra* flower is better] than that *arka* flower.
A leaf of the *dvailva* tree, a *campaka* flower, and a lotus.
One *droṇa* each of *dhuttūraka*, *kuśa*, *śamī*, *apāmārga*, and *utpala*,
increasing by one thousand [units] respectively.
The blue lotus is the most excellent of flowers.
On the earth, on the mountain peaks, in the midst of the sky, in the netherworlds, and in the world of the gods—

gave the Ocean of Milk to him who sought milk.
May the reality of all the Vedāntas, as well as that of the Purāṇas and indeed of all the Śāstras, shine forth fully within you.
"O son of an ascetic, may you possess imperishability.
Having granted these and other boons, the Lord vanished in an instant.
Having then obtained the boon from Śambhu, Upamanyu, the beloved of Śiva,
as well as the great sage Gautama, worshipped Mahādeva.
Practicing all the vows of Śiva, he was beloved by Śaṅkara;
having fully attained all branches of knowledge and the wisdom of Śiva, he remained under the control of his Lord.
Having attained permanence through supreme joy, he remained as one dear to Śiva;
Sadānanda, the lord of yogins, whose conduct is ever-blissful, [attained] the embodiment of Being-Consciousness-Bliss.
Having worshipped Maheśvara himself, together with Ambā, with supreme devotion,
he wandered continuously through all the worlds and even through the various planes of existence.
Having thoroughly understood the events in each of those places, the ascetic,
with supreme joy, reported everything daily to Śambhu.
Having offered obeisance according to the prescribed rite to the dweller of Kailāsa,
he became like an ocean of waves of supreme bliss.
(p. 497) The Life of Mārkaṇḍeya:
The great sage Mṛkaṇḍu, having worshipped Mahādeva, obtained as his son Mārkaṇḍeya, who was proficient in all branches of knowledge.
Having attained complete renown throughout the worlds by means of that,
he dwells forever in Satyaloka with supreme joy.
The son of Mṛkaṇḍu was the wise and great sage Mārkaṇḍeya;
O Lord of Gods, since this one of great asceticism was obtained by Mṛkaṇḍu from you.
Then the sage was conceived by Śambhu at the age of sixteen;
sixteen years passed for him in due succession.
O brahmins, when only two days remained for Mārkaṇḍeya,
his parents, seeing that death was imminent, wept bitterly.
And having heard of their calamity caused by himself,
the son of Mṛkaṇḍu [approached] Virūpākṣa, the conqueror of Death, the destroyer of heroes, the wielder of the Pināka bow.
The meritorious soul, with his mind intensely fixed on that alone, performed worship;
at that moment, Antaka (Yama) quickly arrived there before the son of Mṛkaṇḍu.
O Brahmins, he summoned his own people with affectionate words;
devoted to the worship of Śiva, he remained there, disregarding Yama at that time.
Then, assuming a terrifying form, he who was of fearsome appearance embraced that sage— who stood in the form of a *liṅga*— out of fear, frightening him with his great and swelling bulk.
And when Vaivasvata drew him away, having bound him with a noose,
then the Blessed Maheśvara manifested from that liṅga.
The Lord swiftly struck that terrifying Yama with his foot;
by the force of the Lord's kick, this Yama fell far away.
O Brahmins, he who resembled a great mountain reportedly died;
then, opening his eyes, the son of Mṛkaṇḍu beheld him nearby.
And he beheld before him Mahādeva, the destroyer of Time, the wielder of the Pināka bow, resembling a blue mountain and with his life-breath departed.
The great sage Mārkaṇḍeya praised Nīlakaṇṭha, the odd-eyed one, adorned with a crown of matted hair, with supreme devotion.
Salutations to you, the Death of Death, the three-eyed one who wields the trident;
to you who transcend the universe, who are the universe itself, and who are higher than the highest.
Salutations to you, the one with matted hair, the formidable one, who is fond of the dance of Kālī;
salutations to the fierce, the all-consuming, the terrifying, and the great one.
"Salutations to you, O swift-arrowed one; salutations to you, the destroyer of heroes.
Having heard this praise from that great-souled one, Mahādeva—
The Gracious One, the Soul of the Universe, spoke to the great sage Mārkaṇḍeya:
"O great sage Mārkaṇḍeya, I am pleased with your worship."
O Sage, may you always live for sixteen more years;
and all that you desire shall be accomplished without delay.
Having thus granted him the boon, the Lord vanished on the spot;
and that great sage Mārkaṇḍeya, having attained eternal life, [remained there].
Having reached his own home, he lived forever with his parents with the greatest affection;
he was peerless in the world and an expert in the scriptures of Śiva.
Even today, he remains fully endowed with the knowledge of the meaning of the Śiva-āgamas.
The Account of Agastya (Śaṃkara Saṃhitā, Upodghāta 79):
Agastya, the lord of ascetics, [honored] Śambhu with worship.
The Lord of Ascetics took away the pride of the great mountain Vindhya.
He caused the ocean, agitated by swarms of waves of pride, to drink [the poison];
likewise, he disciplined the two evil-minded ones, Celvala and Vātāpi.
By the grace of the Lord, he composed the language known as Dravidian;
the ascetic attained complete and perfect mastery of all the scriptures.
O twice-born ones, he beheld the supreme *tāṇḍava* dance of the God of gods;
he beheld the auspicious and purifying presence of Śambhu together with Pārvatī.
He accomplished the difficult feat of traveling at will to all the worlds;
likewise, he received instruction in Śiva-yoga from Skanda.
He attained world-wide renown and became highly honored by all the world.
The Story of Dadhīci:
The meritorious Dadhīci,
whose wealth was his asceticism, also established a friendship with King Kṣupa from his very childhood.
Once, this Brahmin and the king engaged in a dispute;
the king declared the power of kings to be superior, while the Brahmin asserted his own power to be so.
O twice-born ones, when the debate between those two had thus proceeded in many ways,
the king, his own superiority being challenged by the disputant, struck him in anger.
Then that evil-souled king, possessed of a wicked mind, took up a terrifying thunderbolt and struck the brahmin in his wrath.
Then that ascetic gave up his life due to the blow of the thunderbolt;
there was a great cry of "Alas! Alas! among those present, which was terrifying.
Then Śukra, his grandfather, quickly arrived;
that descendant of Bhṛgu reunited his body which had been split in two.
O brahmins, the wise one restored him to life by means of his own knowledge;
seeing that his grandson was alive, Śukra spoke these pleasing words to him.
From this day forward, worship of the Great Lord must be performed by you;
through the worship of the God of gods, everything shall be yours.
Worship bestows merit upon men; worship of the Lord bestows liberation. Through worship, Brahmā attained his own station, and Viṣṇu attained the state of a Vaiṣṇava.
Indra, Yama, as well as Īśāna, Kubera,
and the other lords of the gods [worship] that non-dual Maheśāna, the conqueror of death, the companion of Umā.
(500) Calamities, enemies, diseases, and malevolent planets come to an end;
the mind attains clarity when Maheśvara is worshipped.
Having spoken thus and instructed him regarding many Manus, Bhārgava departed quickly according to his own will, O lords of the Brāhmaṇas.
Then the meritorious Dadhīci, worshipping the Lord Śaṅkara,
[requested] the state of having adamantine bones, invincibility, magnanimity, and fearlessness.
Having obtained [these] from the gracious Lord of the Gods, that bull among sages,
having received other boons as well, approached the presence of Kṣupa.
Then the king, agitated by anger, took up a terrifying thunderbolt and struck that evil-minded Kṣupa with his foot.
And the one of great strength struck Dadhīca in the middle of the chest.
O twice-born ones, it quickly turned into dust right there upon falling.
Smiling, Dadhīci, of great ascetic merit, said to that Kṣupa:
"O protector of the earth, I do not fear even your thunderbolt weapon."
"I do not consider even Īśāna to be a match for you, much less your creator.
Upon hearing Dadhīci’s words, Kṣupa became intensely agitated with anger.
Aiming for Viṣṇu, he performed a very great and difficult penance;
as he was thus performing intense austerity, Hari himself appeared before him.
Having bowed to him, the king related his own story to him;
having heard that, Hari went with him to the hermitage of Dadhīci.
Having seen the best of sages there, he honored him with supreme joy.
"O best of ascetics, speak thus to the kings regarding this unsurpassed army for my sake: 'Whatever fault may arise from this, let it fall upon me.'"
When he did not accept these words of Mādhava,
Hari, agitated by anger, hurled his terrifying discus at him.
As it fell upon him, the discus turned to dust in an instant;
yet the illusory Hari produced manifold illusions against that sage.
O Brahmins, he [the sage] dispelled all that illusion of his by means of his own power;
then, that lord of sages also created an illusion upon him.
Taking up another blade of darbha grass, the sage hurled it at him;
at that very moment, he caused all the armies of the enemy of Madhu to perish.
At that time, Hari himself remained all alone;
oh, even then Brahmā, the best among the knowers of Brahman, arrived there.
He praised Dadhīci, the best among those who practice austerity, with supreme joy;
meanwhile, Dadhīci, seeing Viṣṇu standing before him, looked upon him with anger.
"O Viṣṇu, the exceedingly powerful Vīrabhadra shall cut off your hand;
for these devotees of yours, out of great folly, have reviled the Supreme Lord."
"May those who rely upon the Pañcarātra fall into a terrible hell!"—
while the sage was thus cursing Viṣṇu, Brahmā spoke to him in anger.
A quarrel with the devotees of Śiva will fall upon you yourself;
furthermore, O Hari, victory shall not be yours, for you are the offender.
Having thus suddenly summoned Janārdana,
Brahmā, the Supreme Lord, bowed to the sage and, after consoling him, departed.
When the Lotus-born [Brahmā], along with Nārāyaṇa, had then departed for his world,
Kṣupa, beholding that sight, was struck with wonder at this Dadhīca;
he sought refuge in him alone, saying again and again, "Forgive me!"
O best of Brahmins, you were formerly my friend, and today you are my father;
you are my honored mother and brother; indeed, O twice-born one, you are everything to me.
To him who was entreating, "Forgive my offense," he replied:
"O King, it has already been forgiven by me; for the virtuous have forgiveness as their very essence."
For those like me, O King, prostration is the remedy for anger;
for Brahmins are powerful, since he is the lord of our lineage.
The Great Brahmin is remembered as Īśāna; Viṣṇu is the sovereign of the Kṣatriyas; Brahmā is the lord of the Vaiśyas; therefore, they are [designated] as Brāhmaṇas and so forth.
Since even sinners and outcasts perform sacrifices by transgressing [this path],
you should therefore worship Hara and become a lover of Brahman.
O King, the splendor of Brahman is superior, not that of the Kṣatriya born of the Vaiśya;
for the Blessed Lord Śiva is the highest of all because he is a Brāhmaṇa.
He whose deity he is—that Brāhmaṇa is also great among the great;
therefore, one should always offer salutations to Brāhmaṇas day after day.
If you are wise, O Kṣupa, best of kings, you should never speak ill of them;
rule the earth with justice.
Having thus taken leave of that lord of the earth,
Dadhīci returned once more to his devotion to the worship of Śiva and was filled with wonder.
Meditating upon Maheśāna alone, he passed a hundred years;
likewise did Brahmā, Hari, and the gods headed by Mahendra.
Through the very greatness of the worship of Śiva,
the highly fortunate sages— renowned and firmly established in Brahman— attained union with Śiva.
They attained liberation from the bonds, which is difficult even for the wise to achieve;
yet the notion that those other than Śiva are equal to Śiva is fraught with danger.

But for sinners who pride themselves on the knowledge of equanimity, a mind superior even to that of Śiva arises toward another deity for the sake of their destruction. In whomsoever the Lord is pleased, in him devotion shall flourish.
One should not trust that person in whom there is neither the grace of the Lord nor the nature of a wicked man.
Just as the acquisition of a lamp serves only to increase the darkness for one who is blind,
devotion to Śiva does not arise in one who is a vessel for what is unwholesome.
Teaching the Dharma to the ignorant is like pouring water on sand;
teaching the Dharma to the wise is like providing irrigation for a field.
If a wise person places trust upon hearing the words of authoritative scripture,
he partakes of the fruits as described and indeed attains the world of Śiva.
One who lacks faith, is full of doubt, and has lost his discernment regarding all undertakings will be indecisive;
therefore, he perishes.
For one who has placed trust, even a single means of proof may be sufficient to yield the result; however, for one who does not trust, numerous proofs do not bear fruit.
When a mango seed is sown, through protection such as watering and so forth, even a single one bears fruit at will; let this be demonstrated with haste.
Even when seeds are sown everywhere many times, they do not bear fruit for men due to a lack of trust; having observed this, the wise person should place their trust [in the right recipient].
Some were slain by the curse of Dadhīci, others by the curse of Gautama,
and still others, possessed of sinful minds, were destroyed by the curse of Kaṇva.
Those who are averse to the worship of Śiva and the hymns of praise to Śiva become partakers of suffering;
others are ruined through the loss of their intellect, while still others are destroyed by delusion.
Others, ruined by pride in their own doctrines, are indeed sinners;
some even say, "My father was devoted to another doctrine, so I have not come here."
Others have perished through fear of the country; others are struck down by obstacles;
others are terrified by powerful hatred and are turned away from the power of Śiva.
Due to their attachment to wealth and their kinship ties, others deceive themselves;
struck down by poverty as a result of the sins they have previously accumulated, they are undone by their own actions.
Out of greed for seizing wealth, these sinful others have perished;
all of them, by the power of the Kali age, have been destined for the abode of hell.
Formerly, at the request of Yama and by the command of Śambhu, the Gaṇas turned mortals away from Śiva and caused them to dwell in hell.
They perform it, yet they do not know that Śiva is the bestower of liberation;
even the ignorant say that the fruit of worshipping Śiva is worldly prosperity.
(504) For the wise indeed say that there is no other fruit of worship in this world than this:
a husband should cause his wife, who desires a son, to eat the middle *piṇḍa*.
All of them, without distinction, were born from the body of Rudra.
Those whose minds are afflicted by evil do not recognize their father at all;
yet this very Veda, with its clear syllables, remains awake and declares the truth.
One should know that the son who hates his father is one born from another's seed;
those mortals who hate Śiva are born from the seed of another.
"Clearly, you are not born from a single seed, nor do you arise from various seeds among the gods"— this mantra expresses the worship of Śiva.
Furthermore, those who are devotees of Śiva are declared to be the best of Brāhmaṇas;
for Śambhu is proclaimed as Brahman, and he who knows Him is remembered as a true Brāhmaṇa.
This devotee of Śiva is a Brāhmaṇa; no other is called a Brāhmaṇa.
Whether of twice-born (dvijāti) or other birth, one is such solely through devotion to Śiva.
A person is called a *brāhmaṇa* by the virtuous never on account of devotion to another [deity],
but rather he who possesses devotion for Śiva and worships Him according to the prescribed path—
he is Śambhu himself, worshiped by all; this is the truth, the absolute truth, there is no doubt.
Whoever reads this book, listens to it, or even causes others to hear it, he alone shall be a Vīraśaiva; let this be observed with careful attention.

Thus ends the fourteenth instruction, titled the Chapter on the Worship of Śiva, in the *Kriyāsāra* composed by the venerable Nīlakaṇṭhaśivācārya, who was a master of the one hundred and one secret points of the glorious Viśiṣṭādvaita doctrine.
